summary: The repeat of the client-contract revision (receipt 108a83830e904d90a9236738033c2c74) reproduced every outcome: the committed entry is truncated after healing (violated, witness 7), the FSMs diverge after the acknowledged write (violated, witness 7), and the stale leader confirmed leadership while the old majority led in term 4 (violated, witness 6, verify_ok true), so the VerifyLeader consequence is reproducible rather than a scheduling accident. The interpretation cites that receipt, records it as counterevidence, and now counts four executions in which the stale leader still led when the competing leader appeared, against the one harness revision that saw it step down first. I also recorded honestly that the third repair path — a later configuration entry restoring a stale node through processConfigurationLogEntry — remains source-established only, since in the empty-configuration cases the repairs requiring a leader cannot start and in the stale cases the node that would receive such an entry is itself the leader computing changes from the stale base.
